title: The Delhi Red Fort Car Blast Case
dek: A car exploded near Delhi's Red Fort in November 2025, killing at least 11 people in what authorities called a terror attack tied to a Kashmir-based module. Chargesheets naming ten accused followed within months, but the trial itself has barely begun.

heroStat.label: people killed when a car exploded near the Red Fort on November 10, 2025

promise.quote: This is a terrorist act, and those responsible, and everyone linked to the conspiracy, will be identified and brought to justice.
promise.madeBy: Government of India / Ministry of Home Affairs
promise.role: Union government, on designating the blast a terror incident
promise.context: Made two days after a car exploded in slow-moving traffic near the Red Fort in Old Delhi, after which the National Investigation Agency (NIA) took over the probe under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

target.description: A swift, thorough NIA investigation identifying the full conspiracy and network behind the attack, leading to a credible prosecution.
target.standard: Government's own designation of the case as a terror investigation under UAPA, which carries an expectation of a time-bound chargesheet process.

reality.description: The NIA identified the driver, Dr Umar Un Nabi, who died in the blast, as linked to Ansar Ghazwat-ul-Hind, an affiliate of Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent, and to a wider module of doctors and associates allegedly running a 'white-collar terror' cell across Jammu & Kashmir, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh. Arrests reached eleven people by February 2026. NIA filed a 7,500-page chargesheet against ten accused on May 14, 2026, followed by a supplementary chargesheet on June 27, 2026 naming further accused, citing over 580 witnesses. As of August 2026, the trial court was still deciding whether to take cognisance of the chargesheet — the case had not yet moved to trial proper, roughly nine months after the blast.

gap.metricLabel: Days from blast to court taking cognisance of the chargesheet
gap.targetDisplay: ~90 days (typical UAPA chargesheet-to-cognisance expectation for a high-profile case)
gap.actualDisplay: ~290 days (blast Nov 10, 2025 to cognisance hearing Aug 27, 2026), and cognisance itself still pending
gap.note: There is no single statutory deadline for a court to take cognisance; the 90-day figure is this entry's estimate of a reasonably swift benchmark for a high-priority terror case, not a legal requirement, and is flagged as such.

timeline.label: Car explodes near Red Fort
timeline.detail: A car explodes in traffic near Delhi's Red Fort, killing at least 11 people and injuring more than 20; officials suspect ammonium nitrate-based explosives.

timeline.label: Case declared a terror attack
timeline.detail: The Indian government designates the blast a terrorist act; the NIA takes over the investigation under UAPA.

timeline.label: First arrest
timeline.detail: NIA arrests a Kashmir resident, Amir Rashid Ali, alleged to have conspired with the driver.

timeline.label: Arrests reach eleven
timeline.detail: NIA arrests two more individuals linked to the alleged conspiracy, taking the total number of arrests to eleven.

timeline.label: First chargesheet filed
timeline.detail: NIA files a 7,500-page chargesheet against ten accused, citing more than 580 witnesses.

timeline.label: Supplementary chargesheet
timeline.detail: NIA files a supplementary chargesheet naming further accused, including an absconding paediatrician, taking the total accused to 13.

timeline.label: Cognisance hearing
timeline.detail: The trial court is scheduled to decide whether to take cognisance of the chargesheet, roughly nine-and-a-half months after the blast.

legalStatus.summary: This is a stub entry. Ten accused were chargesheeted in May 2026 with a supplementary chargesheet in June 2026 naming further individuals; as of publication the case had not yet moved past the cognisance stage to trial, and presumption of innocence applies to all named individuals.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: the investigation into the blast moved relatively fast by Indian standards — arrests within days, chargesheets within roughly six months — but the case had not reached trial as of nine months after the attack, and this entry has not yet tracked whether that pace continues once trial begins.
verdict.reasoning: This entry was added to place a significant 2025-26 domestic security incident in the site's timeline, drawn from NIA statements and contemporaneous reporting. It has not yet been updated with any trial-stage developments beyond the cognisance hearing.

incomplete: This entry has not tracked the case beyond the August 2026 cognisance hearing; whether and when a trial formally began is not yet reflected here.
The full list of accused and their specific alleged roles, beyond the driver and a handful of named individuals, has not been detailed here.
Any question of whether wider institutional failures (e.g. in vetting or surveillance) contributed to the plot going undetected has not been assessed in this entry.
